evaluation_questions.context: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) is the agricultural policy of the European Union. It implements a system of agricultural subsidies and other programs. It was introduced in 1962 and has undergone several reforms since then. The CAP accounts for about one-third of the EU's total budget. Its main objectives are to improve agricultural productivity, ensure a fair standard of living for farmers, stabilize markets, assure availability of supplies, and ensure reasonable prices for consumers. Recent reforms have focused on making agriculture more environmentally sustainable and shifting payments from production-based subsidies to direct income support for farmers.
